reason_for_amendment: Forward finite-sigma semantics were frozen after v1: an underresolved capillary wall layer now fails closed rather than automatically substituting a sigma-to-zero outer solution.
The mathematical sigma-to-zero outer solution remains available only through the explicit solve_capillary_singular_limit API and must be labelled as an asymptotic reference.
Resolved finite-sigma convergence therefore requires a coupled sigma/radial-grid sequence, while deliberately underresolved cases are expected failures.

v3_amendment.interpretation: The four-interval floor is necessary, not sufficient; residual and refinement evidence remain mandatory.
reason_for_amendment: The frozen candidate replaced the preliminary l_c/dr >= 0.05 check with the declared necessary sampling floor l_c/dr >= 4, i.e. at least four uniform output intervals per capillary length.
The lowest-sigma resolved sequence point therefore increases from 512 to 640 radial points; old v1/v2 remain immutable audit records.

amendments.n64_role: expected UnderresolvedSurfaceError counterexample, never a convergence datum

reason_for_amendment: Applying v3's four-interval capillary floor shows that the v1 radial-grid level n=64 is not an admissible finite-sigma discretisation at the default parameters (l_c/dr approximately 3.80).
The representative finite-sigma radial sequence must contain only admissible grids; n=64 remains covered separately as an expected underresolution counterexample.

A dry run showed that at W=0.1--0.4 the backend nonlinear-minus-linear O(W^3) correction is smaller than the declared collocation/output-grid error and its quotient cannot be certified from the production discretisation.

The W^3 hard asymptotic check is therefore assigned to the independent high-accuracy BVP route; the backend must instead approach its linear baseline at weak forcing, while its unresolved cubic coefficient is retained as a negative resolution result.
Independent BVP refinement changes far below the solve tolerances are classified tolerance-limited equivalent rather than falsely requiring a signed monotone sequence.
